problem_type: Director feature flag bootstrap IPC blocks first window
symptom: Flag-off read-only reload walk timed out at Electron launch on the feature branch while origin/main opened normally.
direct_cause: preload invoked ipcRenderer.sendSync for the cross-process feature proof before first navigation; the normal sender guard required stable frame and origin URLs and never returned during bootstrap.
class_root: A synchronous preload bootstrap call reused a post-navigation IPC trust boundary whose URL-dependent checks are unavailable until the first page has loaded.
migration: Keep the cross-process fingerprint handshake, but route only this pre-navigation channel through a bootstrap guard that verifies the registered main window identity and role.
affected_population: Every Electron startup that loads the preload feature proof, especially the flag-off read-only walk and dev harness startup
invariants: The feature flag is still resolved by both processes and fingerprints must match.
Bootstrap IPC accepts only the registered main window webContents.
Post-navigation IPC channels retain the URL and frame trust checks.

door_reduction.why_not: The preload call and main registration are separate sides of the cross-process boundary and both remain explicit.

residual_risks: CI Linux timing still needs the next Canvas Acceptance run; local branch and origin/main timing evidence covers the reproduced startup regression.
internal_only_reason: This is an internal Electron startup ordering and sender-guard invariant.

recurrence.reason: Any future synchronous preload call made before navigation can hit the same URL-dependent guard if it is registered through the normal IPC helper.

generality_proof: The bootstrap helper centralizes the only pre-navigation exception and leaves every normal channel on the existing strict guard.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Validate bootstrap sender identity and return the synchronous IPC envelope.
Accept only the registered main window before frame URL stabilization.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Feature proof uses the dedicated bootstrap channel and fingerprint mismatch disables the flag.
All other synchronous channels continue to call assertTrustedSender.

prevention.invariant: Pre-navigation synchronous IPC must use the bootstrap sender guard.
prevention.failure_mode: Unregistered or non-main senders receive an error envelope and cannot provide a feature proof.
prevention.exception_policy: Only the feature proof channel is registered through this helper.
prevention.strategy: Keep bootstrap trust narrow and separate from post-navigation origin trust.

legacy_paths.rationale: No legacy implementation was removed; the existing strict guard remains for normal channels.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No dependency controls this startup ordering invariant.
